subject: CAIQ artifact sampling & in-scope ownership plan (vendor review)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@lumenhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: CAIQ control in-scope artifacts for Redwood - vendor review

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our procurement and security teams are starting the vendor review for Redwood and we need a concise CAIQ mapping and a small set of sample artifacts for in-scope controls to validate during the security assessment. Specifically, could you provide: 

- A CSV mapping of the CAIQ/CCM control IDs we discussed to Redwood-specific evidence artifacts (e.g., logs, runbooks, contracts).
- Sample artifacts for a representative subset of controls: access control (IAM proofs), runtime telemetry/logs (anonymized), and change-management evidence.
- A point of contact on your side for questions and a target delivery date (we're hoping for something within 7 business days if possible).

HubSpot ticket for reference: HS-987612

If there are any constraints on sharing logs (PII/PHI), please advise on redaction or sanitized extracts we can accept.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Senior Security Program Manager
Lumen Health

---
Note: cc'd security@lumenhealth.com for scheduling
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: CAIQ control in-scope artifacts for Redwood - vendor review

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear ask and the HubSpot link. We're able to support this. I'm looping in Priyom (security/compliance lead) and Marcus (SRE/ops) to own the artifacts. Proposed plan: 

1) By EOD Tue (2025-07-08) we'll send: 
   - CAIQ-to-artifact mapping CSV (controls -> artifact filenames/locations)
   - A small artifacts bundle (sanitized logs, access matrix, change-doc sample) as ZIP or Drive link
2) Priyom will attest to any redaction/PHI constraints and provide redaction notes.
3) Marcus will prepare an anonymized runtime log sample and retention metadata.

If that timeline works for you we'll proceed. If you need a shorter turnaround, let us know which controls are highest priority so we can sample those first.

Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Compliance (interim)
Redwood Inference

[Redwood Inference | redwoodinference.com]
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jul 2025 08:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: CAIQ control in-scope artifacts for Redwood - vendor review

Thanks Kim / Marta — quick update from my side:

- Attached (access_matrix_20250706.csv) is a preliminary access matrix mapping IAM roles to control IDs for the CAIQ subset you flagged (IAM, access review, privileged access). The CSV includes owner names and the location of the supporting artifact (Drive path or archive name).
- For logs: we can provide a one-hour span of runtime telemetry (request traces, auth events) with IPs and user IDs redacted. We'll include a redaction_notes.txt that lists what was redacted and why.
- Change management: we will include a representative PR and release note package showing approvals and timestamps.

Notes / caveats: 
- Log exports will be sanitized; we can provide a checksum for the sanitized bundle for integrity checks.
- Any artifact that may contain PHI will be replaced with a generated example and a signed attestation describing the procedures we use in production.

Marcus, please confirm the expected Drive location and ETA for the runtime logs sample. Marta, does a sanitized one-hour sample plus the CSVs meet your review team's needs, or do you need longer windows?

- Priyom
Senior Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Looping back — I can produce the runtime log bundle and will sanitize per Priyom's notes. Planned contents: 

- sample_runtime_logs_20250707.zip (request traces, auth events, anonymized session ids)
- kv_cache_snapshot.txt (shows caching behavior for inference requests)

One operational note: the runtime traces include request metadata for troubleshooting (latency, tokens). If you need only access events (auth/no request payloads) say the word and I will pare them down further.

Marcus Lin
